## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A four-fascicle Northern-Sòng Chinese translation of the *Udānavarga* in pure verse-form — without the prose-commentary that accompanies [T212](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0069). Compiled by [法救](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%95%91) Dharmatrāta and translated by [天息災](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E6%81%AF%E7%81%BD) Tiānxīzāi (also known as Devaśāntika) at the Northern-Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn*. Signature: 「尊者法救集／西天中印度惹爛駄囉國密林寺三藏明教大師賜紫沙門臣天息災奉詔譯」.

**Abstract**

T213 is the third Chinese *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* in the canon, alongside [T210](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0067) and [T212](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0069). It represents the late-tenth-century Northern-Sòng re-translation of the verse-only *Udānavarga* recension, with no prose-commentary; the text follows the 33-chapter structure of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (cf. Bernhard's edition). The translation can be dated to Tiānxīzāi's documented Northern-Sòng activity (980–1000) at the Imperial Translation Bureau under [Sòng Tàizōng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E5%AE%97%E8%B6%99%E7%82%85) 太宗.

The Indic source corresponds closely to the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* recension preserved in the Turfan / Central-Asian manuscript fragments; T213 is therefore an unusually late and stylistically refined witness for that recension.
